topPRs.title: interop: replace superseded Lagoon upgrade-transaction spec with the NUT bundle
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
`specs/interop/derivation.md` is Lagoon's derivation page (`protocol/lagoon/overview.md` links to it; there is no `protocol/lagoon/derivation.md`). Its "Network Upgrade Transactions" section still described the pre-bundle design and contradicted the generic mechanism specified in `l2-upgrades-1-execution.md`.

## What was stale

**Enumerated four individual deposits** generated from a nightly contracts commit (`71c460ec`), carrying a "will be updated once a contracts release is made" note. Lagoon activates via a 28-transaction NUT bundle (`lagoon_nut_bundle.json`).

**Used the pre-bundle gas model** — `MaxResourceLimit + SystemTxMaxGas + UpgradeGasUsage ≤ L2GasLimit`, requiring every upgrading chain to set `L2GasLimit > 24_320_000`. That directly contradicts [iUBGL-003](https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/l2-upgrades-1-execution.html#iubgl-003-gas-limit-independence-from-block-gas-limit), which requires the allocation to be independent of the block gas limit and to work "even if block gas limits are set to minimum values".

**Described the wrong activation timing** — CrossL2Inbox proxy initialization as a separate event on "the first block at or after the activation block" for chains in a multi-chain dependency set. The dependency-set-conditional transactions execute *in* the activation block, wrapping the bundle.

## Changes

**`specs/interop/derivation.md`** — describe the bundle, mirroring `karst/derivation.md`. Adds:

- *Dependency Set Conditional Transactions* — the two wrapper deposits (`setFeature(INTEROP)` at 100,000 gas before the bundle, `ETHLiquidity` funding at 50,000 after) emitted only by chains in a multi-chain dependency set.
- *Upgrade Block Gas Limit* — points at the generic mechanism and states that the allocation must not vary with the dependency set.

**`specs/protocol/l2-upgrades-1-execution.md`** — the gas *bump* was specified, but not its reversal. Adds:

- *Reverting the Allocation* — reconstructing the system config from the activation block MUST subtract the allocation, so the next block returns to the steady-state gas limit; the subtraction precedes any same-block `SystemConfig` update from the L1 origin; reconstruction MUST fail rather than wrap if the gas limit is below the allocation.
- An allocation condition requiring the amount to depend only on the fork. The reversal is computed from the rollup config and a timestamp alone, so an amount that varied with the dependency set could not be reversed correctly — a chain would either leak the wrapper gas onto every later block or over-subtract it.

That last point is not hypothetical: op-node and kona had implemented opposite halves of it and disagreed by exactly 150,000 gas from the first block after activation. Fixed in ethereum-optimism/optimism#22216.

## Incidental

- `scripts/upgrades/interop.sh` generated the removed per-transaction sections and is now dead — it pinned the same nightly commit as the removed prose. Removed, and `scripts/README.md` (which used it as its worked example, and whose copy command already named a non-existent file) now walks through `upgrades/jovian.sh`, which is still on the generator path.
- `karst/derivation.md`: the intent prefix is `Karst <index>: `, not `Karst: `; the bundle link's display text and href named different files, and it pinned a commit where the surrounding specs use `develop`.

## Verification

`markdownlint` 0 errors, `cspell` 0 issues, doctoc regenerated, filename lint clean. All cross-references checked to resolve. Transaction counts, gas values, intent strings, and orderings verified against the monorepo bundles and `op-node/rollup/derive` at `eaef4492c8`.

topPRs.title: lagoon: exclude post-exec transactions from DA footprint
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Exclude Lagoon post-exec transactions (`0x7D`) from Jovian DA footprint accounting.

- Specify zero contribution to block `daFootprint` and receipt `blobGasUsed`.
- Explain the late-construction tradeoff and the bounded, linear underestimate for the version-1 SDM payload.

Context: ethereum-optimism/optimism#22101

## Validation

- `just lint-specs-md-check`
- `npx cspell specs/protocol/lagoon/post-exec.md`
- `just lint-filenames-check`
- `just lint-specs-toc-check`
- `mdbook build`
- `lychee` on `specs/protocol/lagoon/post-exec.md`

topContributors.summary: claude: Focused on structuring and expanding the documentation framework for the Optimism ecosystem, notably merging PR #22184 to establish tab skeletons and indices for App Developers and Chain Operators. They also initiated work on the OP Mainnet "keep-and-grow" documentation via PR #22185, contributing over 160 lines of new content and configuration. Their efforts this month were dedicated entirely to improving the information architecture and accessibility of technical docs.

joshklop: Focused on enhancing the reliability of the op-reth node by addressing data consistency during initialization. They initiated work on a significant update to recover proof history gaps on startup (ethereum-optimism/optimism#22177), contributing over 360 lines of new code. This effort included a substantial focus on testing to ensure the robustness of the recovery mechanism. Their primary focus this month was on improving node stability and data integrity within the optimism ecosystem.

oplabs-renovate: Focused on maintaining system integrity by initiating several critical security updates across the infrastructure and optimism repositories. The work involved opening six security-focused pull requests to address vulnerabilities in dependencies such as quic-go (infra#696), brace-expansion (infra#695), and various pion modules (optimism#22181, #22180, #22179, #22178). These efforts highlight a primary focus on proactive dependency management and security patching.

sbvegan: Focused on quality assurance and peer feedback this month, contributing two pull request approvals. Their activity centered on reviewing the work of others to ensure code standards were met. Overall, their primary focus was on supporting the development pipeline through the review process.

harshinsecurity: Focused on enhancing the robustness of block processing within the optimism repository, specifically by addressing unhandled payload statuses in the op-node. They authored a significant update in PR #22182 (+94/-4 lines) to ensure the system rejects invalid statuses during the CommitBlock phase. This work involved a balanced effort between core code logic and comprehensive test coverage to validate the new error-handling behavior. Their primary focus this month was on improving the reliability and security of the node's consensus layer through rigorous testing and validation.

antoine-wak: Focused on expanding token availability within the ecosystem by initiating the integration of the WAKU token on the Base network. This effort is represented by an open pull request in ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io (#1345), which involves adding necessary configurations to the platform. Their primary focus this month was centered on ecosystem configuration and asset integration.

NexusAther: Focused on expanding the ecosystem's asset support by initiating the integration of wRATR (Wrapped Ratatoskr) on the Base network. This work is currently captured in an open pull request within the ethereum-optimism.github.io repository (#1346), which involves adding necessary configurations to the platform. Their primary focus this month was centered on infrastructure and configuration updates to support new token listings.

Flotapponnier: Focused on enhancing project documentation by contributing a new benchmark reference for the OP Mainnet RPC. They initiated this work through an open pull request in ethereum-optimism/optimism (#22183), which integrates OpenChainBench data into the existing documentation. Their primary focus this month was exclusively on documentation updates.
